arguments.title: De-duplicate order pricing without changing behaviour
arguments.spec:
# Refactor: De-duplicate Order Pricing Without Changing Behaviour

`src/pricing.mjs`'s `applyOrderPricing` and `src/invoicing.mjs`'s `renderInvoiceTotals` both compute order
totals over a shared discount ladder and region tax table, written out verbatim in both files, and
`applyOrderPricing` does validation, summing, discounting, taxing and shipping all in one function body.
Restructure the code; do not change what it does. `src/index.mjs` must keep exporting `applyOrderPricing` and
`renderInvoiceTotals` by those exact names -- the public surface is part of the behaviour being preserved.

`scenarios/`, `test/refactor.test.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are FROZEN evidence, digest-checked on every
run. Two things are measured on every run: BEHAVIOUR (every frozen scenario must still pass, exactly as
before) and STRUCTURE, graded against exactly two goals in `refactor/manifest.json`'s `refactor/goals.json`:

- G1 `no_duplicate_block` -- no run of 6 substantive source lines may appear in two different files under
  `src/`. Verified against the real fixture: the unmodified tree already fails this (the discount-ladder and
  tax-lookup blocks are byte-identical between `src/pricing.mjs` and `src/invoicing.mjs`).
- G2 `max_function_lines` -- no function may exceed 30 meaningful lines (comments and blank lines do not
  count). Verified against the real fixture: the unmodified tree already fails this too --
  `renderInvoiceTotals` is 41 meaningful lines and `applyOrderPricing` is 52, both over the limit.

The deliverable is `refactor/manifest.json`: `addressed` lists the goal ids genuinely met; every goal you list
is checked immediately and strictly, so listing one that is not met is worse than listing nothing. `complete:
true` requires every goal to be listed and met. The declared acceptance command (`npm test`) must pass exactly
as-is, offline -- never add a dependency.

One repair, hand-verified against the real fixture to satisfy both goals at once while leaving all 8 frozen
behaviour scenarios passing unchanged: extract the shared discount ladder, region tax lookup and rounding
helper into their own modules (used by both `pricing.mjs` and `invoicing.mjs`), and split `applyOrderPricing`
into small named helpers in the same file. `invoicing.mjs`'s own line-summation loop stays as it is today (it
does not validate lines, and must not start doing so) -- only the discount, tax and rounding logic is shared.
arguments.plan:
Two cards, chained:

1. `dedupe-and-shrink-pricing-rules` -- does the actual restructuring (new src/rounding.mjs, src/discount.mjs,
   src/tax.mjs; pricing.mjs split into small helpers; invoicing.mjs pointed at the shared modules). Verified
   empirically against the real fixture: all 8 behaviour scenarios (B01-B08) still pass, and claiming both G1
   and G2 against the refactored tree is genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier (no duplicate-block
   hits, both functions and all new helpers at or under 30 meaningful lines). This card lists both goals in
   refactor/manifest.json's `addressed` (leaving `complete: false`) once it has verified them itself via a real
   npm test run in-session.
2. `verify-and-complete-pricing-refactor` (depends on 1) -- independently re-verifies (does not trust the
   previous card) that both goals are genuinely met via a fresh npm test run, then sets `complete: true`.

Plan: one card extracts the shared discount/tax/rounding logic into their own small modules and splits applyOrderPricing into named helpers -- verified empirically against the real fixture to satisfy both structural goals at once while keeping all 8 frozen behaviour scenarios passing exactly as before; one card independently re-verifies and marks the manifest complete. No open assumptions.

tasks.title: De-duplicate the discount/tax rules and shrink applyOrderPricing
tasks.prompt:
Restructure src/ to remove the duplicated discount-ladder and region-tax logic between
src/pricing.mjs and src/invoicing.mjs, and bring every function (old and new) to 30 meaningful lines or fewer.

Baseline (verified against the real fixture, not assumed): claiming both G1 and G2 against the UNMODIFIED tree
fails -- 6 reported duplicate-block hits between src/invoicing.mjs and src/pricing.mjs in the discount-ladder
region (there is more duplication than the 6 shown; the failure message caps at 6 hits), plus
`renderInvoiceTotals` at 41 meaningful lines and `applyOrderPricing` at 52 (limit 30 for both). The tax lookup
(6 lines, `let taxRate = 0; if (region === "eu")...`) is ALSO byte-identical between the two files -- fix it
too, even though it may not appear among the first 6 reported hits.

Shape (verified empirically against the real fixture: all 8 frozen behaviour scenarios B01-B08 keep passing
exactly as before, and both G1 and G2 are genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier):

- New `src/rounding.mjs` exporting `round(value)` -- the existing two-decimal rounding
  (`Math.round((value + Number.EPSILON) * 100) / 100`), moved here unchanged, used everywhere money is rounded.
- New `src/discount.mjs` exporting `discountRateFor(subtotal, order)` -- the volume-rate-plus-loyalty-rate
  ladder, capped at 0.2, moved here unchanged from either module (they are byte-identical today).
- New `src/tax.mjs` exporting `taxFor(taxable, region)` -- the region tax lookup (eu 0.21, us 0.07, else 0),
  returning the ROUNDED tax amount via the shared `round`, moved here unchanged.
- `src/pricing.mjs`: keep exporting `applyOrderPricing` with the exact same name and signature. Split its body
  into small helpers in the SAME file: `sumLines(lines)` (the validating summation that throws `TypeError` on a
  non-numeric quantity/unitPrice and `RangeError` on a negative one, message unchanged, naming the offending
  sku) and `computeShipping(taxable, shippingSpeed)` (flat 12.5 below 300 taxable, plus 20 for express,
  unchanged). `applyOrderPricing` itself then just calls `sumLines`, `discountRateFor`, `taxFor` and
  `computeShipping` and assembles the result object with the same five fields as before. EVERY function in the
  file, including `applyOrderPricing` itself, must independently be at or under 30 meaningful lines -- the
  limit is measured per function, not just on the export.
  Fields returned by `applyOrderPricing` are your own responsibility to check against every one of scenarios
  B01 through B07 -- their exact field values (subtotal, discountRate, discount, taxable, tax, shipping, total)
  must not move.
- `src/invoicing.mjs`: keep exporting `renderInvoiceTotals` with the exact same name and signature and its OWN
  inline summation loop -- it does NOT validate lines today (no throw on bad input) and must not start doing
  so; route it through the shared `round`, `discountRateFor` and `taxFor` only, not through `sumLines`. Build
  the same three-line `rendered` array as before (`Subtotal:`, `Discount (N%):`, `Tax:`), matching scenario B08
  exactly.
- `src/index.mjs` needs no change -- it already just re-exports `applyOrderPricing` from pricing.mjs and
  `renderInvoiceTotals` from invoicing.mjs, and that public surface must not be renamed or dropped.

Do not change any rounding, discount, tax, shipping or validation VALUE or threshold. Never add a dependency
(the sandbox is offline).
